notes:
Summary: Oryx is a DSP-like adtech platform handling real-time bidding and personalization. Very latency-sensitive: target is P95 <= 20ms for model inference on reranking path during steady-state; acceptable tail under 50ms for short bursts. Cost-sensitive — they want to shrink token/unit cost for peak hours. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization) and a Dedicated pool for predictable throughput.

Key technical constraints / asks:
- Workload: primary reranking model (short context, 64-128 tokens) + personalization embeddings for candidate scoring.
- Traffic profile: steady 800-1200 TPS with 5x spikes during auctions (100ms decision windows).
- Latency SLOs: P50 < 8ms, P95 < 20ms for rerank path; end-to-end decision budget 100ms incl network.
- Throughput goal for POC: sustain 1.2k TPS with <20ms P95 while using quantized models.
- Cost goals: reduce per-inference cost ~30% vs current hosted baseline.
- Model preferences: open Llama-variant 7B for rerank, quantized to int4/int8; fallback to 2.7B if capacity constrained.
- Routing/fallback: multi-tier routing (dedicated -> hosted fallback) and per-route model pinning required.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated user state (expect ~15% cache hit to cut token cost).

Requests from Oryx engineering:
- Redwood to run perf benchmark harness with their traffic replay (we provided s3 replay manifest). Need side-by-side int8 vs int4 vs fp16 numbers and KV cache enabled/disabled.
- Request quantization guidance: which kernels to prefer on A100 vs H100, expected memory & latency tradeoffs.
- Want auto-batching configs and burst scaling examples for Dedicated pools.
